results.answer: 3625 Dyck paths of semilength 10 have bounce path equal to their reversing bounce path. (The counting sequence for n=1..10 is 1, 2, 4, 9, 22, 57, 154, 430, 1234, 3625.)
results.method: Encoded d by east-step heights h; bounce columns are the orbit of 0 under h. Showed bounce = reversing bounce iff h(c-1)<h(c) at every interior bounce column c, giving weight prod C(a_j+a_{j+1}-2, a_j-1) over bounce compositions; summed by transfer DP.

results.answer: All nine simple modules over the trivial extension T = A ⋉ D(A) (a symmetric algebra of dimension 60) have Ω-period exactly 8, so the sum of the Ω-periods is 9·8 = 72.
results.method: Built T explicitly: quiver = linear arrows 1→…→9 plus duals of maximal paths (5→1,6→2,7→4,8→6,9→7); wrote all 9 projectives (dims 6,7,7,8,8,8,7,5,4) and computed minimal syzygies of each simple by hand; every chain closed at Ω^8.

results.answer: Every one of the 9 simple modules over the trivial extension T = A ⋉ D(A) has Ω-period 8, so the sum of the Ω-periods is 9 × 8 = 72.
results.method: Built T explicitly (quiver = A_9 line plus arrows 5→1,6→2,7→4,8→6,9→7 dual to maximal paths), described all 9 projective T-modules basis-wise, then computed minimal projective resolutions of each simple; each returned to itself after exactly 8 steps.

results.answer: All nine simple modules over the trivial extension $T=A\ltimes D(A)$ have $\Omega$-period 8, so the sum of the $\Omega$-periods is $9\cdot 8=72$.
results.method: Built the quiver of T (linear quiver plus arrows from the bimodule socle paths [1,5],[2,6],[4,7],[6,8],[7,9]), lifted to the repetitive algebra, and computed minimal projective resolutions of all 9 simples; each returned the same simple after 8 steps (4 copy-shifts).

results.method: Identified A as quiver on triangle {(i,j)}_{1<=i<=j<=5} with aa=bb=0, ab+ba=0, rad^3=0, gldim 4; derived Ext^i(M,A)=0 criterion (only P(k,5) non-injective), classified spherical simples (12); full indecomposable count estimated.

results.answer: There are 75 distinct Luna types for representations of Q of dimension vector d=(1,3,4,1), taken over all stability conditions θ admitting semistables.
results.method: Enumerated decompositions d=Σ m_i d^i into distinct Schur roots admitting a common θ with θ·d^i=0, using sink (vertex 3) / source (vertex 4) forcing θ3≤0, θ4≥0, splitting by the {2,3}-supported components (all S2, or all proportional to a primitive (p,q)), and checking generic-subrepresentation stability inequalities case by case.

results.answer: There are 75 distinct Luna types for representations of Q of dimension vector d=(1,3,4,1), taken over all stability conditions admitting semistables (including the trivial type {(d,1)} and the fully-simple type {(S1,1),(S2,3),(S3,4),(S4,1)}).
results.method: Computed Euler form, Schur roots ≤ d, the semistable cone (a 3-dim cone over a quadrilateral with rays (-1,0,0,1),(2,-1,0,1),(0,4,-3,0),(4,0,-1,0)), then enumerated all decompositions d=Σ m_i e_i with e_i simultaneously θ-stable.

results.answer: 84 distinct Luna types occur for Q with d=(1,3,4,1) over all stability conditions admitting semistables (counting a Luna type as a multiset of pairs (stable dimension vector, multiplicity)).
results.method: Listed Schur subroots of d; used sink/source subrepresentation and Schofield ext criteria to get exact stability inequalities (θ3>0, θ4<0, q>-c/b etc.); enumerated θ in the 2-dim space d^perp by cases (one summand at vertex 1, one at 4, middle summands of fixed slope), then counted multiplicity partitions: 1+16+62+5=84.

results.answer: 84 distinct Luna types. (A Luna type is a datum {e: partition} with e a θ-stable Schur root and Σ|p^e|·e = (1,3,4,1); the union over all θ admitting semistables, including θ=0, has 84 members.)
results.method: Enumerated Schur roots ≤ d via Tits form, computed generic sub-dimension vectors (Schofield) to get θ-stability inequalities, then classified all decompositions d=Σ m_i e_i admitting a common θ, decorating repeated summands by partitions.

results.answer: There are 75 distinct Luna types for representations of Q of dimension vector d = (1,3,4,1), taken over all stability conditions θ admitting semistable points.
results.method: Enumerated multisets Σ m_i e_i = d realizable as simultaneous θ-stable dimension vectors, using King stability, sink/source subrepresentation constraints (t3≤0, t4≥0, etc.), generic-subrepresentation analysis, and Schur-root checks; split by sign of t3, t2 and by the pieces carrying vertices 1 and 4.

results.answer: There are 75 distinct Luna types for representations of Q with d=(1,3,4,1), taken over all stability conditions admitting semistables (16 with a single part containing both vertices 1 and 4, plus 59 with separate parts for vertices 1 and 4).
results.method: Enumerated decompositions d=Σm_i e_i with a common θ making each e_i stable, using Schofield's generic-subrepresentation criterion (⟨f,e-f⟩≥0 plus hom computations) to get cone conditions on θ; Kronecker parts are multiples of one primitive, counted by partitions of gcd.

results.answer: The maximum shattered-triple density tends to 5/16 = 0.3125. It is attained (e.g.) by taking, besides the identity and the reverse, the four "bit-reversal" orders of {0,...,2^N-1} obtained by XOR-ing with the masks 11...1, bit0, bit1, and bits>=2.
results.method: Reduced shattering to a 6-colouring of pairs by edges of K4 (matching class m + bit s); good triple iff m(ab)=m(bc)!=m(ac), s(ab)!=s(bc). Optimized recursive (dyadic) constructions; best found 1/4+1/16.

results.answer: The maximum shattered-triple density tends to 1/4 as n → ∞.
results.method: Reduced shattering to: for x<y<z the 4 non-trivial permutations split 2 with x in middle, 2 with z in middle, differing on one adjacent pair. Taking σ3=rev σ1, σ4=rev σ2 gives condition "σ1,σ2 non-monotone with opposite middle types" = 2-coloring condition κ(xy)=κ(yz)≠κ(xz). Construction σ1 = half-rotation, σ2 random gives 2·(3/8)(1/3)=1/4; perturbation/kernel analysis (|s−t| conditionally negative definite) shows 1/4 is optimal.

results.answer: The maximum density of shattered triples tends to 5/16 = 0.3125.
results.method: Reduced shattering to a 6-colouring of pairs by edges of K_4 (3 antipodal pairs): need class(ab)=class(bc)≠class(ac) with opposite signs. Optimal periodic (mod 4) difference construction gives 20/64; dyadic sign constraint caps sum at 1/4+1/16.

results.answer: The maximum density of shattered triples tends to 1/4. It is attained by a self-similar 3-block "rotation" family {id, rev, σ, rev∘σ, τ, rev∘τ} (σ, τ cyclic shifts by n/3, 2n/3, recursed inside blocks), giving density 2/9 + (1/9)ρ = 1/4.
results.area: Extremal combinatorics of permutations (shattering / VC-type densities)
results.method: Reduced shattering to "three medians distinct" = rainbow pair-coloring; proved D = 1/4 − (3/4)∫(f−g)² ≤ 1/4 identity; matching recursive 3-block rotation construction.
